# leghorn

> A full-screen live dashboard you leave open on a second monitor while many Claude
> Code sessions work: every live session joined to its worktree and real git state,
> your GitHub CI and open PRs with failures pinned until they go green, and a commit
> feed across every repo, newest first.

Two files, stdlib-only Python 3.9+. Runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows (curses via
windows-curses on Windows). Read-only by construction: it reads session transcripts,
runs `gh` and read-only git plumbing, and never writes to a tree, a registry, or a
session.

## What it's for

Anyone running several Claude Code sessions against several git worktrees loses track
of two things a per-session view can't show: which worktrees are shared by more than
one session (silently destructive — two sessions in one checkout can overwrite each
other's uncommitted work) and which CI runs or PRs need attention across every repo at
once. leghorn ranks the GitHub pane by what it costs to ignore — running first, then
red (a failure must not scroll away), then stuck-in-queue, then everything else by
freshness. Every data source is optional; a missing piece degrades to a labelled gap,
never an error.

## Install

- Homebrew (macOS/Linux): `brew install gmhoward9289-ops/tap/leghorn`
- npm: `npm install -g leghorn`
- Direct download: GitHub Releases

## Links

- Repository: https://github.com/gmhoward9289-ops/leghorn
- README (full usage, install matrix, screenshots): https://github.com/gmhoward9289-ops/leghorn/blob/main/README.md
- License: Apache-2.0
- Related tool: roost (https://github.com/gmhoward9289-ops/roost) — a live dashboard
  focused on model/context-window/subagent state per session, complementary to
  leghorn's focus on git/worktree state and GitHub CI.
